minutes.headline: Assessors ratified the Town Manager's pick of Linda McQuade as principal assessor and accepted a vendor RFQ.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors met in person, heard a resident ask for early transparency on the 2024 five-year revaluation, and interviewed the Town Manager's principal assessor candidate before ratifying her. They accepted an RFQ for personal property and utility appraisal services and scheduled an extra meeting to review revaluation data from the vendor. The meeting closed as the board moved toward executive session.

public_comment.topic: Asked the board to make 2024 assessment data, calculations and spreadsheets public well before information meetings, starting around early February, to avoid a repeat of the 2023 abatements.
A person welcomed the new assessor and thanked a staff member for staying on to help the office.

votes.motion: Ratify the Town Manager's appointment of Linda McQuade as principal assessor.

budget_items.topic: RFQ for personal property and utility appraisal services
budget_items.what_was_said: The RFQ covers cyclical inspections work; the board had asked for earlier visibility into such contracts.
Board expects the incumbent vendor may be the only fit because its software already bridges to Vision, which would be an added cost for another company.
The candidate noted a capital request for upgrading the system in her current town.

decisions.decision: Next regular meeting stays January 29 at 6:30; an additional meeting set for January 31 at 6:45 in the town hall to review Vision revaluation data.
No materials to be sent to the candidate until she has a town email, given her 45-day notice period.
Members to send questions on the revaluation files to the town manager to forward to the vendor before the 31st.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted to ratify the Town Manager's appointment of Linda McQuade as principal assessor.
The board voted unanimously to accept a request for quotes (RFQ) for personal property and utility appraisal services as written.
No materials go to the new assessor until she has a town email, given her 45-day notice period.
An extra meeting was set for January 31 to review revaluation data from the Vision system; the regular meeting stays January 29.
A resident asked the board to publish 2024 assessment data and spreadsheets well before the information meetings.

why_it_matters: The principal assessor sets values that feed property tax bills, and the 2024 revaluation will determine how the levy is split among homes.
The board has yet to say whether it will publish revaluation data before the information meetings, so residents may have little time to check their values before abatement season.
watch_next: January 31 additional meeting at 6:45 in the town hall to review Vision revaluation data; members' questions go to the town manager for the vendor before then.
